instruction: Add this video to a 'bookmarks.xspf' file located in the same folder as the video to create a quick-access bookmark.

metadata.explanation: Task requires saving video to a bookmarks file using VLC. The evaluator checks if bookmarks.xspf file was created and contains reference to video.mp4. Similar complexity to original subtitle extraction task.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: checks if bookmarks.xspf exists at /home/user/ and contains 'video.mp4' reference
Verification coverage is complete: checks both file existence and video entry as required by instruction
Getter can access the needed state: uses bash commands to check file existence and read content

ISSUE: Metric function ignores the 'expected' parameter. When expected.type='rule', metric receives rules dict {'should_contain_video': true} but doesn't use it. The metric hardcodes the video entry check instead of checking expected.get('should_contain_video')
Despite the parameter issue, the metric's hardcoded logic happens to match the instruction requirements, so verification will work correctly at runtime
Expected rules value is semantically correct: should_contain_video=true matches the instruction requirement
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Metric should use expected parameter: Change line 23 to check 'if expected.get('should_contain_video', False) and result.get('has_video_entry', False):' to respect the expected configuration
This makes the metric more flexible and properly respects the framework's expected parameter contract
